    Your first endpoint in 5 minutes#

    What you need#

    • JDK 25 (LTS). jimble uses virtual threads and ScopedValue
    • Gradle 9 or later. Gradle 8 does not run on Java 25 (8 can target Java 25 as a toolchain, but Gradle itself will not run there)

    You do not need a DB yet. You can add one later.

    Installing the jimble command is covered in The jimble command (run ./gradlew :jimble-cli:installDist in the repository and put it on your PATH).

    1. Create the skeleton#

    jimble new my-blog
cd my-blog
gradle wrapper

    jimble new creates the build files, application.conf, App.java, index.jte, and .gitignore — nothing else. It does not create empty directories.

    2. Start it#

    ./gradlew run

    jimble 構成: env=local / session=none / cache=db / redis=なし / db=[]
route: GET     /
jimble を起動しました: http://localhost:9000

    The startup log prints every route. That is so you catch "the route I thought I registered isn't there" at startup.

    curl http://localhost:9000/

    3. Add an endpoint#

    Add one line to the initializer block in App.java.

    get("/hello", context -> context.response().send("hello, jimble\n"));

    The { } is an initializer block; it runs before the constructor. The initializer block of a class extending JimbleApp is your route definition.

    To return JSON:

    get("/posts", context -> context.response().json("posts", BlogApp.listPosts()));

    json() builds up a Data (a subclass of LinkedHashMap<String,Object>) and turns it into JSON at send() time.

    4. Make your edits show up#

    ./gradlew jimbleRun

    jimbleRun puts a proxy on port 9000 and starts your app behind it, inside the same JVM. When you edit a source file, it builds and swaps it in on the next request. If the build fails, you see that error in the browser.

    See Hot reload for the details.

    5. Decide how errors come out#

    error((context, cause, statusCode) ->
	context.response().code(statusCode).send("エラー: %d %s%n".formatted(statusCode, cause.getMessage())));

    Whatever you pass to error() handles both thrown exceptions and the 404 for a request that matched no route. Register nothing and you get jimble's default shape.
